turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, this computer's frozen on yesterday again. One second. Ok. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): The spots on my face, hey, and my monthlies are all over the show.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has that been going?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Must be two years. My cousin's wedding in Durban, there was this huge cake, and the DJ kept playing...
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, err, say that again? I was on the wrong tab.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): About two years for the pimples and the periods. And these dark hairs on my chin, shame.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you just run late, or do you miss whole months?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I miss them. Sometimes nothing for three months, then it comes heavy and the sheets are a write-off.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): The hair on the chin, when did that start?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, my mum won't drop it. She's got sugar, been on insulin for years, she says I'm headed the same way. Even the parking marshal was...
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, I'm rambling. The hairs, I can't tell you when they started. They're just dark, and at the clothing shop where I work people stare.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. I can see a few coarse hairs on the chin, and comedones on both cheeks. Has the weight gone up?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, same two years, eight-ish kilos I reckon. They weighed me in the passage just now, 79.4. My varsity jeans are a whole story, hey.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the tummy, or have the bowels changed?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No pain, bowels are fine.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): And shortness of breath?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, no. Breathing is fine. I walk to the shop most days.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you on? This list looks ancient.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine 5 milligrams in the morning, that's for the pressure. The cholesterol one at night, atorvastin 20. Sugar tablets, metforman 500 twice a day, for the sugar. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, half a teaspoon, my neighbour at the spice shop says it...
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hold on. Screen jumped. The cholesterol one, dose again?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): 20 milligrams at night. Amlodipine stays 5 in the morning. Nothing else from the chemist.

[SEG0022] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry to butt in, doctor. Her mum's outside. She says the cut on the shin healed in five days, that she sleeps badly, and that she doesn't take the tablets on Sundays.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): That cut. Did it heal normally, or was it slow?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Normal, hey, five days and done, not slow. It's not Sundays, it's Saturdays I skip the cholesterol one, when I go through to my sister in Pietermaritzburg. The sleeping, mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Saturdays then. I'm not putting the sleep down as a clear yes.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): For the note, the weight before she came through was 79.4 kilograms. Blood pressure today is 122 over 78, and the pulse was 76.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): 122 over 78, got it. Thanks, you can go.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Ok, I'll leave the file.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): So, spots, missed periods, chin hair, the weight. I'm thinking polycystic ovarian syndrome, provisional, not confirmed.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that serious? My friend had something and she couldn't...
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not calling it confirmed. I'm booking bloods, the hormones and a glucose, and a pelvic scan. I am not starting a contraceptive pill today.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): The pill? I've never been on one. Umm, my friend says it helps the skin, but with the sugar tablets I don't know.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): We might look at a contraceptive pill if the bloods and the scan fit. Only then. Keep that Ayurvedic powder exactly as it is, and don't add anything new.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): The powder's just in the morning. I don't know the real name, the writing's all faded.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bring the packet next time if you find it. Come back in six weeks and we'll go through the results. Reception will have the blood form and the scan date.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks, ja. Parking out there took me round the block twice, the machine wouldn't take the card...
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Six weeks it is. Packet if you find it.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Sharp, I'll try. Thanks, hey.

spec.situation: Young woman with acne and irregular periods for two years, some facial hair, weight gain; mother had diabetes; bloods and pelvic scan planned; contraceptive pill discussed, not started.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Heavy menstrual bleeding detail missing: when menses come after missed months, they are heavy enough that 'the sheets are a write-off.'
Weight gain quantified as about 8 kg over the same 2-year period.
Medication adherence detail not recorded as a clinical action/history: patient skips atorvastatin on Saturdays when visiting her sister in Pietermaritzburg.
Sleep disturbance was not clearly endorsed; patient said 'sometimes, not really,' and doctor explicitly said not to record sleep as a clear yes.
Doctor specifically said not to start a contraceptive pill today.
Patient stated she has never been on a contraceptive pill.
Planned blood tests were specified as hormones and a glucose test.
Reception will provide the blood form and the scan date.
